title: Canary failure-mode synthesis and hotpatch scheduling notes
content:
Meeting: Canary Failure-Mode Synthesis + Hotpatch Scheduling
Date: 2026-03-09 10:00-11:00 PT (recording in #release-ops)
Owners: Maya Singh (chair)
Attendees: Ethan Park, Luis Ortega, Priya Raman, Anika Patel, Drew Chen (SRE), Claire B. (QE)

Objective:
- Consolidate observed failure modes from the 2026-03-08 canary run.
- Agree immediate mitigations and hotpatch windows.
- Produce an actionable schedule + owners for tomorrow's hotpatch and follow-up investigation.

High-level summary:
- Canary run for release v2.14.1 exposed two recurring failure classes: 1) transient gRPC stream resets during long-tail requests (p95+ tail), 2) degraded KV-cache eviction thrashing when request concurrency spikes. Both resulted in ~3-7% error increase for affected routes and spiky latency on a subset of hosts. Impact scoped to Canary lane only; no customer outages observed.
- Immediate mitigation (rolled in morning): reduce canary traffic to 20% and route long-tail model variants to fallback pod class; this stabilized the error rate but did not eliminate tail spikes.

Context / notes from dashboards:
- Timeline: 03:12 UTC — first error cluster on canary-uk-*-b. 03:17 UTC — spike correlates with batch-size bump from autoscaling event. 03:25 UTC — series of evictions logged on cache-manager at node-level. 03:34 UTC — gRPC reset correlation with network egress queue depth on multi-tenant hosts.
- Relevant signals: p50/p95/p99 latency per host, gRPC reset counts, kernel drop counters (tx-queue-drops), cache-eviction rate, cpu steal on hosts running mixed workloads.
- Quick log excerpt (abbreviated):
  [03:16:52] cache-manager WARN evict: candidates=1200, reclaimed=8, latency=7.2ms
  [03:17:03] infra-gRPC ERROR stream_reset: code=14, conn=10.2.4.88:4231->10.2.4.14:4012
  [03:25:44] host-monitor WARN tx-drop: if=eth0 drops=34 queue_len=512

Observed failure modes (synthesized):
1) gRPC stream resets caused by network egress queuing under bursty traffic + contention with background model downloads. Symptoms: partial response resets, increased retries leading to higher server-side concurrency.
2) Cache eviction thrash: aggressive eviction policy reacting badly to bursty prefix patterns; eviction + re-populate leads to CPU spikes and increased tail latency.
3) Autoscaler-oscillation amplification: short-scale autoscaling events (scale-up then scale-down quickly) interacts with cache heat and KV state leading to warm-cache loss on downscale.

Hypotheses (ranked):
- Most likely root cause combo = network queue pressure (egress) + cache eviction under concurrency.
- Secondary contributor = autoscaler sensitivity with default cooldown=30s (too short for cache warmup).

Immediate mitigations executed (what we did in morning):
- Reduced canary traffic from 100% -> 20% to buy time.
- Toggled model-download background rate limiter (throttled to 50% of normal) on canary hosts.
- Adjusted cache eviction threshold: eviction_target from 0.70 -> 0.80 on canary pool.
- Increased autoscaler cooldown to 120s for canary nodepools.
Outcome: error rate dropped from 6.2% -> 1.1% within 18 minutes; tail latency improved but occasional spikes remain.

Decision: schedule hotpatch vs full rollback
- Consensus: proceed with targeted hotpatch (infra changes) rather than full rollback. Rationale: hotpatch addresses network queueing and eviction policy; rollback would lose canary visibility. If hotpatch fails to reduce spikes to <0.5% error and <25% of pre-hotpatch tail amplitude, revert plan to rollback.

Hotpatch plan (owner assignments + window)
- Window: 2026-03-10 02:00-04:00 UTC (low traffic, cross-check with SRE staffing).
- Steps (runbook checklist):
  1) Preflight: snapshot canary node health, collect p95/p99 baseline, save heap/profile artifacts (Claire).
  2) Apply kernel tx-queue tunables to canary host kubelet config (Drew).
  3) Deploy cache-manager config bump (eviction_target=0.82, background_repopulate=true) as ConfigMap canary-only (Ethan).
  4) Adjust model-download rate limiter in infra-config (Luis) and validate no pending downloads backlog.
  5) Promote autoscaler cooldown change to all canary nodepools (Anika).
  6) Incrementally ramp canary traffic 20% -> 60% over 30m while watching signals (Maya).
- Rollback criteria (explicit):
  - If error rate >2% sustained for 10m after any step, immediately abort and rollback changed configs in reverse order.
  - If p99 latency increases by >40% vs baseline, abort and restore previous configs.
- Post-hotpatch follow-up: run a full 3-hour soak while maintaining 60% traffic; if stable, consider step-up to 100% after 6 hours and SRE signoff.

Risk matrix (quick):
- Risk: Change to kernel tx-queue could affect non-canary services on node. Mitigation: apply only to canary nodepools; SRE to confirm host-selector.
- Risk: Eviction tuning may increase memory usage. Mitigation: monitor OOM trends; preflight mem-snapshot.
- Risk: Autoscaler cooldown increase may temporarily reduce capacity responsiveness. Mitigation: keep an emergency manual scale command ready and allow burst capacity window.

Action items (concrete)
- Ethan: implement and test cache-manager config change in staging. Create PR and link (due 2026-03-09 EOD).
- Luis: throttle model-download background process and document metrics to watch (REL-3421) (due 2026-03-09 16:00 PT).
- Drew (SRE): prepare kernel tx-queue patch script and a rollback helper; run triage on whether `txqueuelen` tweak is sufficient (due 2026-03-09 18:00 PT).
- Claire (QE): produce a reproducible load script (microbenchmark) that replays the observed burst pattern; run against staging config (due 2026-03-10 00:00 UTC).
- Anika: verify canary nodepool selector labels and update autoscaler cooldown to 120s in infra-config (PR and schedule) (due 2026-03-09 20:00 PT).
- Maya: coordinate hotpatch window w/ on-call SRE + product (confirm 02:00 UTC window) and publish runbook in #release-ops (due 2026-03-09 19:00 PT).

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Do we have long-term plan to decouple background model downloads from inference hosts? (Design doc needed) -> assigned to Luis to draft proposal by 2026-03-16.
- Is eviction policy the right knob or do we move to a small LRU-tierper-model cache? Need cost/complexity analysis. -> add to March sprint planning.
- Should we introduce a short circuit at the load-balancer to drop ultra-long-tail requests for canary while debugging? (Pros/cons discussed; need product signoff)

Notes-to-self / meeting scribbles:
- TODO: capture exact kernel settings we changed and baseline as gist.
- Watch list metrics: host.tx_drops, grpc_stream_resets, cache_eviction_rate, p99_lat_ms (route=generate-text), node_oom_kills.
- Logged quick-link to stacktrace blob for one reset event: /artifacts/rt-2026-03-08-reset-4672.log
- Slack thread: #release-ops -> thread ts=1678492020 (see pinned messages)

Appendix: quick reproduction commands for QE
- Load replay: scripts/load-replay --pattern=burst-10s --concurrency=120 --routes=generate-text
- Check host tx drops: kubectl -n infra exec -it node-agent -- cat /proc/net/dev | grep eth0
- Snapshot p95: curl -s dashboard-api/local?p=canary&metric=p95

Closing notes:
- Consensus to run hotpatch tomorrow in the 02:00-04:00 UTC window. Owners above to update PRs and post runbook before 19:00 PT today.
- We will reconvene post-hotpatch: 2026-03-10 06:30 PT for quick status and decide step-up/rollback.

---- end of notes ----
